label: Figure 5.1 Aerobic metabolism
text:
Title: What happens to organic matter in Aerobic Biological Process?
Suspended organic matter -> (Hydrolysis) -> Soluble organic matter; branch from suspended organic matter: Non-biodegradable
Soluble organic matter -> branch: Non-biodegradable; -> Residual biodegradable organic matter
Soluble organic matter -> Bio-oxidation -> CO2, H2O, NH3, Energy, etc.; Oxygen (1-1.42Y)
Soluble organic matter -> Bio-synthesis (Y) -> New heterotrophic Microbial biomass (with Residual biomass)
New heterotrophic Microbial biomass -> Auto-oxidation kd -> CO2, H2O, NH3, Energy, etc; Oxygen (1.42Kd)
Carbonaceous BOD is the sum of oxygen utilized during biooxidation of the organic matter and during auto oxidation of the microbial biomass
ammonia -> nitrite -> nitrate; Oxygen (3.43 g/g) for ammonia->nitrite; Oxygen (1.14 g/g) for nitrite->nitrate
Nitrogenous BOD is the sum oxygen utilized during nitrification of Ammoniacal-N to Nitrite-N and Nitrite-N to Nitrate-N
Source: Dr. Akepati S. Reddy, Thapar Centre for Industrial Research & Development, Punjab (printed below the image)
note: 호기성 대사 경로도: 가수분해→생물산화(산소 1-1.42Y)/생물합성(Y)→자산화(kd, 산소 1.42Kd), 질산화 산소 3.43·1.14 g/g. 캡션은 이미지 아래 본문.

label: Figure 5.2 Anaerobic metabolism
text:
Title: What happens to organic matter in Anaerobic Biological Process?
Suspended organic matter -> (Hydrolysis) -> Soluble organic matter; branch: Non-biodegradable
Soluble organic matter -> branch: Non-biodegradable; -> Residual biodegradable organic matter
Soluble organic matter -> Bio-reduction -> CH4, H2O, H2S, NH3, Energy, etc.
Soluble organic matter -> Bio-synthesis (Y) -> New anaerobic Microbial biomass (with Residual biomass)
New anaerobic Microbial biomass -> Digestion -> CH4, H2O, NH3,
Carbonaceous BOD is the sum of oxygen otherwise needed during biooxidation of organic matter
ammonia -> ammonia -> ammonia
CH4, Methane gas is flammable and has calorific value, but cannot be bottled.
H2S is hydrogen sulphide gas produced from sulphate of water and has smell of rotten egg. Also, H2S can form sulphurous / sulphuric acid, which is corrosive in nature.
Source: Dr. Akepati S. Reddy, Thapar Centre for Industrial Research & Development, Punjab (printed below the image)
note: 혐기성 대사 경로도: 생물환원→CH4·H2S 등, 생물합성→소화→CH4. 하단 메탄·황화수소 설명문 포함. 'Bio-synthesis' 아래 Y는 회전 글자로 판독.

Box 5 -> arrow up to Box 1.

label: Equation (5.32)
text:
S / S0 = 4 a e^(1/2d) / [ (1 + a)^2 e^(a/2d) - (1 - a)^2 e^(-a/2d) ]   (5.32)
in which the term a = sqrt(1 + 4 K θ d)
d : dispersion number (dimensionless) = D/UL = Dθ/L^2
latex: \frac{S}{S_0} = \frac{4 a e^{1/2d}}{(1+a)^2 e^{a/2d} - (1-a)^2 e^{-a/2d}}, \quad a = \sqrt{1 + 4K\theta d}, \quad d = D/UL = D\theta/L^2
note: Wehner-Wilhelm 분산흐름 식 (5.32)와 a, d 정의. 이미지 블록 2개 = 식 본체 + 식번호.

label: Figure 5.53 Nutrient removal processes — Case 1: Modified Ludzack Ettinger (MLE) Process with chemical enhanced settling & Chlorination
text:
Influent -> Anoxic tank (NO3-N, NO2-N -> N2) -> Aerobic tank (NH4-N -> NO3-N, NO2-N) -> Secondary clarifier -> Effluent
Nitrified liquor: recycled from end of aerobic tank to inlet of anoxic tank
Return activated sludge: from secondary clarifier underflow via RAS Pump to anoxic tank inlet; waste sludge line continues out
note: MLE 질소제거 공정도. 'Case 1' 소캡션은 크롭 하단에 일부 보이며 본문에도 있음. 그림 자체에는 화학 침전·염소 설비 표시 없음.

label: Figure 5.53 Nutrient removal processes — Case 2: Bardenpho process with Chlorination
text:
Influent -> Anoxic tank -> Aerobic tank -> Anoxic tank -> Reaeration -> Secondary clarifier -> Effluent
Nitrified liquor: recycled from end of first aerobic tank to inlet of first anoxic tank
Return activated sludge: from secondary clarifier via RAS Pump to influent line; sludge line continues out
note: 4단 Bardenpho 공정도. 소캡션은 이미지 밖 본문. 원문 'Retum' 표기는 'Return'의 인쇄 깨짐으로 보임.

label: Figure 5.53 Nutrient removal processes — Case 3: Bardenpho process with Chlorination
text:
Influent -> Anaerobic tank -> Anoxic tank -> Oxic tank -> Secondary clarifier -> Effluent
Nitrified liquor: recycled from end of oxic tank to inlet of anoxic tank
Return activated sludge: from secondary clarifier via RAS pump to influent line (ahead of anaerobic tank); sludge line continues out
note: 혐기-무산소-호기 3단 공정도(본문 소캡션은 Case 3 'Bardenpho process with Chlorination'으로 표기, 원문 그대로). 전체 캡션 Figure 5.53.

label: Figure 5.61 Algorithm for rehabilitation programme of STPs
text:
Box 1:
- Understand the Importance of and Develop Specific Study Plan for Ascertaining Treatment Efficiency for consent to operate parameters
- Identifying shortcomings for complying with consent to operate conditions
- Ascertaining the adequacy of pump sets Vs process flows at all locations
- Ascertaining the oxygen transfer deficiencies of the aeration system
- Ascertaining the shortfalls in check measurements of laboratory results
- Ascertain safety infrastructure and first aid kit deficiencies
- Verify the responses from higher ups to requests from field staff
-> Box 2: Assemble the STP Team keeping it cute in numbers and with persons known to take initiative <-> Review the causative reports, and arrive at prima facie justifications
-> Box 3: Fact finding mission of the team with all members being present simultaneously at site <-> Interactions within the team to decide on additional scope of insights at field & going through it
-> Box 4:
- Team develops the justifications for required rehabilitations of civil, mechanical and electrical items
- Induction of newer items of works and equipment
- Redundancies in existing system which are draining the budget to waste
- Deletions of items of work, personnel and electrical items with no need
- Priority listing of procurements, works, personnel staffing
- Formulate an Immediate works programme
- Formulate a time bound master programme
<-> (down and back up) Box 5: Competent authority review, debate and accord -> Competent authority sanctions the budget and designates officers
Competent authority review, debate and accord -> Reports justifying the variations if needed and recommending the variants to be sanctioned
Competent authority sanctions the budget and designates officers -> Independent team keeps tag of compliance of rehabilitation work and lists variations needed
Both -> Final box: Joint completion report on aims, objectives, compliances, deviations, deletions & recommendations for future to avoid such contingencies arising again
note: STP 개보수 절차 흐름도. 화살표 방향은 그림대로 기술(Box4와 승인 박스 사이 양방향).

label: Table 5.29 Types of sewage treatment technologies
text:
Type | Objective | Process | Description
 |  | Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR) | This process utilizes a fill-and-draw reactor with complete mixing during the batch reaction step (after filling) and where the subsequent steps of aeration and clarification occur in the same tank. All SBR systems have common steps as (1) fill, (2) react (aeration), (3) sedimentation, (4) decant and (5) idle. For continuous-flow applications, at least two SBR tanks are provided in parallel so that one receives the sewage while the other completes its treatment cycle. Several process modifications have been made in the time durations associated with each step to achieve nitrogen and phosphorus removal.
 |  | Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) | This process is based on several synthetic biofilm carrier elements (patented and non-patented) developed for use in the aeration tank of the ASP and are suspended in the activated sludge mixed liquor in the aeration tank. These processes are intended to enhance the activated sludge process by providing a greater surface area to unit volume of the aeration tank for the additional surfaces for increased microbial population and metabolism and hence, the biomass concentration in the tank and offers the potential to reduce the basin volumes. They are used to improve the volumetric nitrification rates and to accomplish the denitrification in aeration tanks by anoxic zones within the biofilm thickness.
 |  | Fixed bed bio film activated sludge process (FFASP) | This process consists of a series of aerated reactors, filtration units and final polishing units. Plants with extensive root systems are placed on a supporting mesh slightly below the water level in the open aerated reactors and their roots dangling about 1.5 metres into the sewage is claimed to provide a healthy habitat for bacteria and a whole range of other organisms such as protozoa, zooplankton, worms, snails and even fish. As sewage flows through these different ecosystems in each tank, a series of self managing, cascading ecologies are stated to provide a highly robust and efficient system.

label: Figure 6.9 Some of the mechanical mixing systems in digesters
text: Four sketches with text: (1) TURBINE MIXER - Mechanical mixing system: the entire digester contents are subjected to a central vortex based uplift and its all round throw of the liquor at the surface, resulting in hydraulic mixing in all vertical planes. (2) EXTERNAL DRAFT TUBE - combination of a central draft tube with downward turbine & external draft tubes relying on downward hydraulic energy dissipated in the draft tube. (3) DRIVE MOTOR, PROPELLER, DRAFT TUBE, W.L., SLUDGE FEED, SLUDGE TRANSFER, SLUDGE DRAINOFF - multiple downward draft tubes along inner rim with spouted ends to suck in the feed sludge and pump towards the centre and in turn the upward circulation to draft tubes. (4) section + plan with MIXING PUMP - Pumped feed system: liquor withdrawn by pumped suction from the tip of the conical floor and/or near the upper zone and pumped back in multiple tangential pumped ends. Source: WEF Manual of Practice 8.

label: Figure 6.10 Some of the gas based mixing systems in digesters
text: Four sketches: Gas injection mixing system (EXCESS GAS, COMPRESSOR, GAS INJECTION LANCES): gas withdrawn from the roof, compressed and released at the bottom of submerged lances inducing upward swell and mixing. Unconfined Gas mixing system (COMPRESSED GAS MIXING LINE): gas withdrawn from the crown, compressed and released at the conical base of inverted cone floor. Confined Gas lifting system (section + plan with 5 draft tubes): gas released into the bottom of multiple draft tubes, buoyancy induced mixing. Gas mixing chute - The induced gas mixing system: once gas attains a pre-set pressure it is released into the upper chamber inducing syphon based mixing through downward draft tube and floor level lances. Sources: WEF MOP-8; AK Dhussa and VK Jain, NBB/MNRE 2002.

label: Table 9-16 Advantages and disadvantages of septage treatment at sewage treatment plant
text:
Method | Description | Advantages | Disadvantages
Treatment at STPs or Independent septage treatment facility in the vicinity of STPs | Septage is added to the pumping station, upstream manhole or sludge treatment process for co-treatment with sewage sludge. Septage volumes that can be accommodated depend on plant capacity and types of unit processes employed. | Most STPs in India are underutilized and are capable to handle some septage. As skilled personnel and laboratory facilities are available in STPs, easy to operate and maintain. | Potential for STP upset if plants are running at full capacity. Increased sludge treatment cost.

rows: Treatment at STPs or Independent septage treatment facility in the vicinity of STPs

Septage is added to the pumping station, upstream manhole or sludge treatment process for co-treatment with sewage sludge. Septage volumes that can be accommodated depend on plant capacity and types of unit processes employed.
Most STPs in India are underutilized and are capable to handle some septage. As skilled personnel and laboratory facilities are available in STPs, easy to operate and maintain.
Potential for STP upset if plants are running at full capacity. Increased sludge treatment cost.

label: Table 9.17 Advantages and disadvantages of independent septage treatment facility
text:
Method | Description | Advantages | Disadvantages
Treatment at independent septage treatment plants | A facility is constructed solely for the treatment of septage. Treatment generates residuals, i.e., dewatered sludge and filtrate which must be dried composted (dewatered sludge) and properly treated (filtrate) prior to being disposed off. | Provides regional solutions to the septage management. | High capital and operation and maintenance cost. Requires high skills of operation in case of mechanical dewatering.

rows: Treatment at independent septage treatment plants

A facility is constructed solely for the treatment of septage. Treatment generates residuals, i.e., dewatered sludge and filtrate which must be dried composted (dewatered sludge) and properly treated (filtrate) prior to being disposed off.
Provides regional solutions to the septage management.
High capital and operation and maintenance cost. Requires high skills of operation in case of mechanical dewatering.

Oxygen | 5-15% | Periodic turning (windrow), forced aeration (static pile), mechanical agitation with compressed air (mechanical).
Temperature (compost must reach) | 55-65ºC | Natural result of biological activity in piles. Too much aeration will reduce temperature.
pH | 5-8 | Septage is generally within this pH range, adjustments not normally necessary.
Carbon/nitrogen ratio | 20:1 to 30:1 | Addition of bulking material.
